block:
--- Local Space.md ---
Managing spaces | Sharing configuration between spaces
To make configuration and libraries available in every local space, use a [[Meta Space]].

--- Guide/Desktop Setup.md ---
Install and open a space | Install and open a space
Follow [[Install/Desktop]] to download the app for macOS, Windows or Linux. In the dashboard, choose **New space** and select an empty folder, or a folder containing Markdown files you already have.

Open the space and use [[Guide/My First Markdown Page]] to try the editor. [[Local Space]] explains the files Desktop keeps in the folder. Keep the folder’s location somewhere you can find when setting up backups.

--- Install.md ---
Desktop | Desktop
[[Install/Desktop|Download and install Desktop]] for macOS, Windows or Linux. Create a space from an empty folder or open an existing folder of Markdown files. An external Server is optional. You can add [[Desktop Sync]] later to sync content to a server.

[[Guide/Desktop Setup]] covers local spaces, updates and optional synchronization.

--- CLI.md ---
Installation | Configuring spaces
Before using the CLI, connect it to a SilverBullet instance. The CLI stores space configurations in `config.json` in:

* macOS and Linux: `~/.config/silverbullet` (respects `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`)
* Windows: `%APPDATA%\SilverBullet` (a configuration in the previous location, `%USERPROFILE%\.config\silverbullet`, is copied there on first use)
* Anywhere: the directory in `SB_CONFIG_DIR`, when set

[[Install/Desktop|SilverBullet Desktop]] uses the same list, so spaces added in either one show up in both. The directory also holds the `key` that encrypts saved tokens and passwords: do not commit it to a dotfiles repository or sync it between machines.

--- Guide/Desktop Setup.md ---
Install and open a space | Use the same space on other devices
If you want browser access or another Desktop installation to use the same content, you need a SilverBullet Server. You can [[Guide/Server Setup|run one yourself]] or use a hosting provider.

For an existing local space, open its settings from the dashboard and configure the **Sync** section. To start with a space already on a Server, choose **Join Space**. Follow [[Desktop Sync]] for the supported authentication methods and connection setup, then check that an edit reaches the other device.

This optional synchronization connects your local folder to an external Server. Desktop’s own editor already reads and writes the local folder. There is no browser offline cache to configure between it and its embedded server.
